title: Year 10 Geography — Coastal Ecosystems Exam
title_zh: 地理 · 海岸单元考版
exam_focus: 只覆盖 Term 3 Week 1–5 海岸单元（1.1 环境变化、1.2 海岸过程、1.3 土地利用、2.1 Collaroy–Narrabeen 概况、2.2 East Coast Lows、2.3 开发、3.1–3.2 可持续管理、3.3 海堤争议、4.1–4.3 海岸田野调查、5.1–5.3 印度河三角洲与管理）。按考试形式设计：大量带 stimulus 的现场判读题＋按分值分配的结构化短答，末题对应 20 分 structured response。

questions.topic: A Changing Global Climate · 温室气体
questions.stem: Which group lists only greenhouse gases?
questions.explanation: 温室气体能吸收并再辐射红外线：CO₂、CH₄、水汽、N₂O、CFCs。氧气和氮气占大气 99% 但几乎不吸收红外线，不是温室气体。
questions.source: Yearly Study Guide 2026 · Geography Section I（terms / metalanguage）

questions.topic: A Changing Global Climate · 增强温室效应
questions.stem: The enhanced greenhouse effect refers to:
options: The natural warming that keeps Earth habitable
Extra warming caused by human increases in greenhouse gas concentrations
The cooling effect of volcanic ash
The reflection of sunlight by clouds
questions.explanation: 自然温室效应让地球平均约 15°C 而不是 −18°C，是必需的；『增强』指人类活动额外增加的温室气体让这个效应变强。
questions.source: Yearly Study Guide 2026 · Geography Section I

questions.topic: A Changing Global Climate · 温室效应机理
questions.stem: In the greenhouse effect, which sequence is correct?
options: Long-wave radiation from the Sun is absorbed by the surface
Short-wave solar radiation passes through the atmosphere, is absorbed and re-emitted as long-wave radiation which is trapped
Greenhouse gases reflect short-wave radiation back to space
The ozone layer traps heat near the surface
questions.explanation: 太阳辐射以短波为主，能穿过大气到达地表；地表升温后以长波（红外）向外辐射，被温室气体吸收并再辐射，一部分返回地表。
questions.source: Yearly Study Guide 2026 · Geography Section II（greenhouse effect）

questions.topic: A Changing Global Climate · 碳源与碳汇
questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as a carbon sink?
options: The ocean absorbing dissolved carbon dioxide
questions.explanation: 碳汇是吸收并储存碳的库：海洋、森林、土壤。燃煤、砍伐、反刍动物都是碳源。
questions.source: Yearly Study Guide 2026 · Geography Section I

questions.topic: A Changing Global Climate · 海平面上升
questions.stem: Global sea level is rising mainly because of:
options: More rain falling into the oceans
Thermal expansion of warming seawater and melting of land-based ice
questions.explanation: 两大机制：海水受热膨胀（约一半贡献）+ 陆地冰（冰川、格陵兰、南极）融化注入海洋。注意『海冰融化』不抬高海平面——它本来就浮在水里。
questions.source: Yearly Study Guide 2026 · Geography Section II（sea level rise）

questions.topic: A Changing Global Climate · 海洋酸化
questions.stem: Ocean acidification occurs because:
options: Acid rain falls directly into the sea
Carbon dioxide dissolves in seawater forming carbonic acid, lowering pH
questions.explanation: CO₂ + H₂O → H₂CO₃（碳酸），碳酸释放 H⁺，pH 下降。工业革命以来表层海水 pH 已下降约 0.1（酸度上升约 30%）。
questions.source: Yearly Study Guide 2026 · Geography Section II（ocean acidification）

questions.topic: A Changing Global Climate · 珊瑚白化
questions.stem: Coral bleaching is caused by:
options: Loss of the symbiotic algae (zooxanthellae) due to heat stress, exposing the white skeleton
Too much oxygen in the water
An increase in coral predators only
questions.explanation: 水温持续偏高时珊瑚排出体内的共生藻（虫黄藻），失去颜色和主要能量来源，露出白色骨骼。若高温持续太久，珊瑚会死亡。
questions.source: Yearly Study Guide 2026 · Geography Section II（ocean temperature and coral bleaching）

questions.topic: A Changing Global Climate · 天气图 · 锋面符号
questions.stem: On a synoptic chart, a line with triangles pointing in the direction of movement represents:
questions.explanation: 冷锋用三角符号（▲），暖锋用半圆符号（◗），三角/半圆朝向表示锋面移动方向。等压线是细实线。
questions.source: Yearly Study Guide 2026 · Geography Section I（synoptic charts）

questions.topic: A Changing Global Climate · 天气图 · 高压
questions.stem: An area of high pressure on a synoptic chart is usually associated with:
questions.explanation: 高压中心空气下沉，不易成云致雨，天气稳定晴朗；低压中心空气上升，容易成云降水。
questions.source: Yearly Study Guide 2026 · Geography Section I（skills · synoptic charts）

questions.topic: A Changing Global Climate · FLICC · 挑樱桃
questions.stem: A website says: 'It snowed heavily last winter, so global warming is a hoax.' Which FLICC technique is this?
questions.explanation: 挑樱桃（cherry-picking）：只挑一个短期、局部的天气事件来否定长期、全球的趋势。天气≠气候：单个寒潮不能推翻 30 年的升温趋势。
questions.source: Yearly Study Guide 2026 · Geography Section I（critical thinking · FLICC）

questions.topic: A Changing Global Climate · FLICC · 假专家
questions.stem: A blog cites 'a retired physicist' with no climate science background as proof that CO₂ does not trap heat. Which FLICC technique is this?
questions.explanation: 假专家（fake experts）：用没有相关领域资历的人营造『专家有争议』的假象。判断要看其研究领域、同行评议记录，而不是头衔本身。
questions.source: Yearly Study Guide 2026 · Geography Section I（FLICC）

questions.topic: A Changing Global Climate · 反馈 · 反照率
questions.stem: As sea ice melts, the darker ocean surface absorbs more sunlight, which causes further warming. This is an example of:
questions.explanation: 冰反照率高（反射阳光），融化后露出深色海面吸收更多热量，进一步升温→进一步融冰，是正反馈（自我增强）。
questions.source: Yearly Study Guide 2026 · Geography Section I（critical thinking / climate system）

questions.topic: A Changing Global Climate · 图表判读
questions.stem: A graph shows CO₂ concentration and global average temperature rising together over 150 years. The most defensible conclusion is:
options: CO₂ has no effect on temperature
There is a positive correlation, consistent with CO₂ driving warming
The data proves nothing at all
questions.explanation: 相关不等于因果，但『正相关且与物理机制一致』同时成立时，结论应表述为『与……一致』。只说『证明』错，说『毫无意义』也错。
questions.source: Yearly Study Guide 2026 · Geography Section I（graph interpretation）

questions.topic: A Changing Global Climate · 海岸影响
questions.stem: Which combination most increases coastal erosion risk in eastern Australia?
options: Lower sea level and weaker storms
Higher sea level, larger storm surges and more intense East Coast Lows
questions.explanation: 海平面升高让同样的风暴浪能在更高的基面上起作用；风暴潮叠加、East Coast Lows 增强、海岸带开发增加暴露度，三者叠加才会放大风险。
questions.source: Yearly Study Guide 2026 · Geography（climate change and impacts on coastal environments）

questions.topic: A Changing Global Climate · 温室效应（简答）
questions.stem: Explain, step by step, how the greenhouse effect keeps Earth warmer than it would otherwise be.
questions.answer: Short-wave radiation from the Sun passes through the atmosphere and is absorbed by the Earth's surface, warming it. The surface re-emits this energy as longer-wave infrared radiation. Greenhouse gases (CO2, methane, water vapour) absorb this infrared radiation and re-radiate it in all directions, including back towards the surface. This trapped energy raises the average surface temperature. Without this effect Earth's average temperature would be about -18C instead of about 15C.
questions.explanation: 得分点四步：短波进入 → 地表吸收并发出长波 → 温室气体吸收再辐射 → 结果升温。顺序错或漏掉『再辐射回地表』会扣分。
questions.source: Yearly Study Guide 2026 · Geography Section II（greenhouse effect）

points.t: Short-wave solar radiation passes through the atmosphere and warms the surface
The surface re-emits energy as long-wave (infrared) radiation
Greenhouse gases absorb and re-radiate infrared back towards the surface
The result is a higher average surface temperature than without the atmosphere

criteria.t: States that short-wave solar radiation passes through the atmosphere and is absorbed by the Earth's surface
States that the warmed surface re-emits the energy as longer-wave infrared radiation
Explains that greenhouse gases absorb the outgoing infrared radiation and re-radiate it in all directions, including back towards the surface
Concludes that the trapped energy raises the average surface temperature, so Earth is warmer than it would be without the atmosphere

questions.topic: A Changing Global Climate · 自然 vs 增强（简答）
questions.stem: Distinguish between the natural greenhouse effect and the enhanced greenhouse effect.
questions.answer: The natural greenhouse effect is a process that has always operated: naturally occurring greenhouse gases trap some outgoing infrared radiation and keep the average surface temperature around 15C, which makes life possible. The enhanced greenhouse effect is the additional warming caused by human activities that increase greenhouse gas concentrations - burning fossil fuels (CO2), agriculture and livestock (methane), and deforestation. The mechanism is identical; what differs is the extra quantity of greenhouse gases and therefore the extra trapped energy.
questions.explanation: 关键在『机理相同、量不同』。只写『一个是自然的、一个是人类造成的』拿不到满分，要指出多出来的温室气体导致额外截留的能量。
questions.source: Yearly Study Guide 2026 · Geography Section II

points.t: Natural: naturally occurring greenhouse gases trap infrared and keep average temperature near 15C
Enhanced: extra greenhouse gases from human activity (fossil fuels, agriculture, deforestation)
Same mechanism, greater quantity of gases, therefore additional trapped energy

criteria.t: Defines the natural greenhouse effect as naturally occurring greenhouse gases trapping outgoing infrared and keeping the average surface temperature near 15C
Identifies the enhanced greenhouse effect as the extra warming from human activities that raise greenhouse gas concentrations (fossil fuels, agriculture and livestock, deforestation)
Explains that the mechanism is identical and the difference is the greater quantity of greenhouse gases, and therefore the extra trapped energy

questions.topic: A Changing Global Climate · 海平面上升（简答）
questions.stem: Explain the two main mechanisms of sea level rise and describe two impacts on the Australian coast.
questions.answer: First, thermal expansion: as seawater warms it expands and takes up more volume. Second, melting of land-based ice (glaciers, Greenland, Antarctica) adds water to the ocean. (Melting sea ice does not raise sea level because it already displaces its own weight.) Impacts: increased coastal erosion and shoreline retreat during storms; inundation of low-lying areas and infrastructure; saltwater intrusion into estuaries and coastal groundwater; loss of beaches and wetlands; greater damage from storm surges.
questions.explanation: 机理必须两项（热膨胀 + 陆地冰），并注意海冰不算。影响要落到澳洲海岸的具体后果（侵蚀、淹没、咸潮、湿地丧失）。
questions.source: Yearly Study Guide 2026 · Geography Section II（sea level rise）

points.t: Thermal expansion of warming seawater
Melting of land-based ice adding water to oceans
Two valid impacts on the Australian coast (erosion, inundation, saltwater intrusion, wetland loss, storm surge damage)

criteria.t: Explains thermal expansion: warming seawater expands and takes up more volume
Explains that melting land-based ice (glaciers, Greenland, Antarctica) adds water to the ocean
Describes one valid coastal impact, such as erosion and shoreline retreat, inundation of low-lying land and infrastructure, or greater storm-surge damage
Describes a second, different coastal impact, such as saltwater intrusion into estuaries and groundwater, or loss of beaches and wetlands

questions.topic: A Changing Global Climate · 海洋酸化（简答）
questions.stem: Explain how ocean acidification occurs and why it threatens marine life.
questions.answer: The ocean absorbs about a quarter of human CO2 emissions. Dissolved CO2 reacts with water to form carbonic acid (CO2 + H2O -> H2CO3), which releases hydrogen ions and lowers the pH of seawater (ocean acidification). The extra hydrogen ions combine with carbonate ions, reducing the carbonate available to organisms. Corals, shellfish and plankton need carbonate to build calcium carbonate shells and skeletons, so their growth slows and shells can dissolve, weakening reef structures and food webs.
questions.explanation: 三步：吸收 CO₂ → 生成碳酸、pH 下降 → 碳酸根减少、钙化受阻。最后要落到生物后果（珊瑚、贝类、浮游生物）。
questions.source: Yearly Study Guide 2026 · Geography Section II（ocean acidification）

points.t: Ocean absorbs CO2 which forms carbonic acid, lowering pH
Fewer carbonate ions available for calcification
Corals/shellfish/plankton cannot build or maintain shells and skeletons

criteria.t: Explains that the ocean absorbs human CO2, which forms carbonic acid and releases hydrogen ions that lower the pH of seawater
Explains that the extra hydrogen ions combine with carbonate ions, so less carbonate is available to organisms
Explains that corals, shellfish and plankton need carbonate to build calcium carbonate shells and skeletons, so growth slows and shells can dissolve
Explains the consequence for marine life: reef structures and food webs are weakened

questions.topic: A Changing Global Climate · 珊瑚白化（简答）
questions.stem: Describe the process of coral bleaching and explain the conditions under which a reef can recover.
questions.answer: Corals live in symbiosis with zooxanthellae, algae that live in their tissue, give them their colour and supply most of their energy through photosynthesis. When water temperatures rise well above the summer average (or the coral is stressed by pollution or extreme low tides), the coral expels the zooxanthellae. The coral tissue becomes transparent, showing the white calcium carbonate skeleton - bleaching. If the stress is short and temperatures return to normal, the coral can take up algae again and recover over weeks to months. If the heat stress persists, the coral starves and dies, and recovery can take a decade or more.
questions.explanation: 要写清『共生藻供给能量与颜色』这一环，否则解释不了为什么会死。恢复条件 = 热压力及时解除 + 水质好。
questions.source: Yearly Study Guide 2026 · Geography Section II（ocean temperature and coral bleaching）

points.t: Corals depend on symbiotic zooxanthellae for colour and most of their energy
Heat stress causes the coral to expel the algae, exposing the white skeleton
Recovery requires stress to end quickly and water quality to be suitable
Prolonged stress leads to starvation and death of the coral

criteria.t: Explains that corals live in symbiosis with zooxanthellae, which give them their colour and supply most of their energy
Explains that heat stress causes the coral to expel the zooxanthellae, so the tissue becomes transparent and the white skeleton shows
States that recovery requires the stress to end quickly and the water quality to be suitable
States that prolonged stress means the coral starves and dies, with recovery then taking a decade or more

questions.topic: A Changing Global Climate · 天气图判读（简答）
questions.stem: A synoptic chart shows a cold front approaching the NSW coast from the west, with a low pressure centre to the south and a high pressure system over the Tasman Sea. Predict the weather change over the next 24 hours and explain your reasoning.
questions.answer: Before the front arrives: warm, moist north-westerly winds ahead of the front, rising temperature and humidity, increasing cloud. As the cold front crosses: a narrow band of heavy rain, thunderstorms, a sharp temperature drop and a wind shift from north-west to south-west, with a rapid rise in pressure afterwards. After the front passes: cooler, drier air, clearing skies and settled weather as the high moves in, with cold nights.
questions.explanation: 判读套路：锋前（暖湿、气压下降）→ 过境（暴雨、降温、风向突转）→ 锋后（干冷、转晴、气压回升）。每一项都要对应图中的要素。
questions.source: Yearly Study Guide 2026 · Geography Section II（synoptic charts）

points.t: Ahead of the front: warm, humid, increasing cloud, falling pressure
At the front: heavy rain/thunderstorms, sharp temperature drop, wind shift
Behind the front: cooler, drier, clearing skies, rising pressure

criteria.t: Predicts that ahead of the front it is warm and humid with increasing cloud and falling pressure, driven by moist north-westerly winds
Predicts that as the cold front crosses there is a narrow band of heavy rain and thunderstorms, a sharp temperature drop and a wind shift, followed by a rapid rise in pressure
Predicts that behind the front it becomes cooler and drier with clearing skies and settled weather as the high moves in

questions.topic: A Changing Global Climate · FLICC 反驳（简答）
questions.stem: Someone posts: 'Climate has always changed, so this is natural. Scientists are only saying this to get more funding.' Identify the two FLICC techniques used and write a short, accurate rebuttal.
questions.answer: The two techniques are: (1) cherry-picking/oversimplification - 'climate has always changed' ignores the rate and the different driver (natural cycles such as orbital change operated over tens of thousands of years, whereas current warming tracks the added greenhouse gases and is far faster), and (2) conspiracy theory - claiming scientists are motivated by funding rather than evidence. Rebuttal: natural factors alone cannot reproduce the observed warming of the last century, particularly the pattern of stratospheric cooling alongside tropospheric warming, which is the fingerprint of greenhouse gases. Scientific claims should be assessed on evidence and mechanism, not on assumed motives; the funding accusation is not evidence.
questions.explanation: 评分看两点：准确指出两种手法名称 + 给出基于证据的反驳。只骂人不给证据拿不到分。
questions.source: Yearly Study Guide 2026 · Geography Section I（critical thinking · FLICC）

points.t: Identifies cherry-picking/oversimplification and conspiracy theory
Explains what the cherry-picking ignores (rate and driver of current warming)
Examines evidence or the fingerprint pattern rather than motives

criteria.t: Identifies cherry-picking (or oversimplification) in the claim that climate has always changed
Identifies conspiracy theory in the claim that scientists are only saying this to get more funding
Gives an evidence-based rebuttal, e.g. natural factors alone cannot reproduce the observed warming and the stratospheric cooling with tropospheric warming is the greenhouse gas fingerprint

questions.topic: A Changing Global Climate · 缓解 vs 适应（简答）
questions.stem: Define mitigation and adaptation in relation to climate change and give one Australian example of each.
questions.answer: Mitigation reduces the causes of climate change by cutting greenhouse gas emissions or increasing carbon sinks - for example building large-scale solar and wind generation and retiring coal-fired power, or protecting and restoring coastal wetlands as a carbon sink. Adaptation reduces vulnerability to the effects that can no longer be avoided - for example building sea walls and dune restoration programs at Collaroy-Narrabeen, or planning retreat zones and raising building floor levels.
questions.explanation: Mitigation = 减少 cause（减排/增汇）；Adaptation = 降低 impact（防护/回避）。例子要落到澳洲、最好落到海岸。
questions.source: Yearly Study Guide 2026 · Geography（climate change responses）

points.t: Mitigation defined as reducing emissions/increasing sinks
Adaptation defined as reducing vulnerability to impacts
One valid Australian example of each

criteria.t: Defines mitigation as reducing the causes of climate change by cutting emissions or increasing carbon sinks
Defines adaptation as reducing vulnerability to the effects of climate change that cannot be avoided
Gives one valid Australian example of mitigation, such as large-scale solar and wind generation or protecting and restoring coastal wetlands as a carbon sink
Gives one valid Australian example of adaptation, such as sea walls and dune restoration at Collaroy-Narrabeen or planning retreat zones

questions.topic: 环境变化 · 变化的速度与尺度
questions.stem: Stimulus: A beach can lose a large volume of sand during a single East Coast Low, while a dune system may migrate inland over thousands of years. What does this comparison illustrate?
options: That all coastal change is gradual rather than sudden
That coastal change is caused only by human activity
That environmental change operates at different rates and scales
That erosion is permanent and that deposition never occurs anywhere
questions.explanation: 环境变化的时间尺度与空间尺度是 1.1 的核心概念：单次风暴可在数小时内改变海滩，沙丘迁移则需千年。两者并存，说明「变化」要按速率与尺度分别描述。
questions.source: Term 3 · Lesson 1.1 Environmental Change（rate and scale of change）

questions.topic: East Coast Lows · 天气图判读
questions.stem: Stimulus: A synoptic chart shows tightly packed isobars and a closed low-pressure centre just off the NSW coast, with a cold front crossing the coast. What does this chart indicate, and why does it matter for Collaroy–Narrabeen?
options: A high-pressure ridge, bringing calm seas and steady offshore winds
An East Coast Low, bringing heavy rain and large erosion-driven waves
A stationary front producing no wind and no coastal impact
A tropical cyclone tracking inland across the ranges from the west
questions.explanation: 密集等压线＝气压梯度大＝强风；闭合低压＋冷锋＝东海岸低压，带来暴雨、强风与大浪。这正是 2016 年该海滩遭受严重侵蚀的天气背景。
questions.source: Term 3 · Lesson 2.2 Understanding East Coast Lows（synoptic map）

questions.topic: 管理策略 · 预防／缓解／准备
questions.stem: Which set correctly matches the three management categories taught in Lessons 3.1–3.2?
options: Prevention — stopping change; mitigation — reducing impact; preparedness — planning response
Prevention — planning response; mitigation — stopping change; preparedness — reducing impact
Prevention — reducing impact; mitigation — planning response; preparedness — stopping change
All three categories describe the same action taken at different scales
questions.explanation: prevention 从源头避免（如禁止在前丘新建）、mitigation 减轻已发生变化的冲击（如海堤、补沙）、preparedness 为事件做准备（如预警与疏散）。分类决定评价标准，别混用。
questions.source: Term 3 · Lessons 3.1–3.2 Sustainable Management of Coastal Ecosystems

questions.topic: East Coast Lows · 2016 事件的机制
questions.stem: Stimulus: A synoptic chart shows tightly packed isobars and a closed low off the NSW coast with a cold front crossing the coast. Explain why this system produced such destructive conditions at Collaroy–Narrabeen in 2016. (3 marks)
questions.answer: Tightly packed isobars mean a steep pressure gradient and therefore strong winds, which generate large waves and a storm surge that raises water levels at the shore. The cold front adds intense rainfall and runoff, so the combination of higher water and bigger waves produced a major storm cut and foredune erosion.
questions.explanation: 机制链：密集等压线→强风→大浪＋风暴增水；冷锋→暴雨。三者叠加正好赶上涨潮，才造成破坏性侵蚀。只写「风很大」拿不到满分。
questions.source: Term 3 · Lesson 2.2 Understanding East Coast Lows

criteria.t: Explains that tightly packed isobars mean a steep pressure gradient and therefore strong winds
Explains that the strong winds generate large waves and a storm surge that raise water levels at the shore
Explains that the cold front adds intense rainfall and runoff, so the combination of higher water and bigger waves produced a major storm cut and foredune erosion

questions.topic: 管理策略 · 分类与理由
questions.stem: Classify each strategy as prevention, mitigation or preparedness, and justify your choice: (a) zoning that prevents new building on the foredune; (b) a seawall; (c) an evacuation plan. (3 marks)
questions.answer: (a) Prevention — it removes the exposure before damage can occur. (b) Mitigation — it reduces the impact of wave energy on assets that already exist. (c) Preparedness — it plans the response for when an event happens.
questions.explanation: 判断依据是「作用于变化之前／之中／之后」：预防在源头避免暴露，缓解降低既有资产的受损程度，准备安排事件发生时的应对。
questions.source: Term 3 · Lessons 3.1–3.2 Sustainable Management of Coastal Ecosystems

criteria.t: Classifies the zoning strategy as prevention and explains that it removes the exposure before damage can occur
Classifies the seawall as mitigation and explains that it reduces the impact of wave energy on assets that already exist
Classifies the evacuation plan as preparedness and explains that it plans the response for when an event happens

questions.topic: 海堤争议 · 立场评估
questions.stem: Stimulus: Two stakeholders disagree about the Collaroy–Narrabeen seawall. One argues it protects homes; the other argues it damages the beach and shifts erosion along the coast. Evaluate both positions using your knowledge of coastal processes. (5 marks)
questions.answer: The protection argument is valid in the short term: the wall prevents wave attack on the houses immediately behind it. The criticism is also valid: a vertical wall reflects wave energy, removes sediment from the beach budget and can increase erosion at the ends of the wall, so the beach in front narrows and the problem shifts along the coast. The decision therefore trades protection of private assets against the loss of public beach.
questions.explanation: 评估题要「两边都成立＋说明代价」：短期保护有效，但过程代价（反射、输沙收支改变、侵蚀转移）真实存在。只站一边不给高分。
questions.source: Term 3 · Lesson 3.3 The Controversial Seawall（stakeholder perspectives）

criteria.t: Explains the protection argument: the wall prevents wave attack on the houses immediately behind it, so it is valid in the short term
Explains that a vertical wall reflects wave energy back onto the beach
Explains that the wall removes sediment from the beach budget, so the beach in front narrows
Explains that erosion can increase at the ends of the wall, so the problem shifts along the coast
Reaches an evaluative judgement that the decision trades protection of private assets against the loss of public beach
